977.name: Dondozo
977.flavor_text: It treats Tatsugiri like its boss and follows it loyally. Though powerful, Dondozo is apparently not very smart.

978.name: Tatsugiri Curly
978.flavor_text: Tatsugiri is an extremely cunning Pokémon. It feigns weakness to lure in prey, then orders its partner to attack.

979.name: Annihilape
979.flavor_text: It imbues its fists with the power of the rage that it kept hidden in its heart. Opponents struck by these imbued fists will be shattered to their core.

980.name: Clodsire
980.flavor_text: It lives at the bottom of ponds and swamps. It will carry Wooper on its back and ferry them across water from one shore to the other.

981.name: Farigiraf
981.flavor_text: The hardened head from the tail protects the head of the main body as Farigiraf whips its long neck around to headbutt enemies.

982.name: Dudunsparce Two Segment
982.flavor_text: It drives enemies out of its nest by sucking in enough air to fill its long, narrow lungs, then releasing the air in an intense blast.

983.name: Kingambit
983.flavor_text: Though it commands a massive army in battle, it’s not skilled at devising complex strategies. It just uses brute strength to keep pushing.

984.name: Great Tusk
984.flavor_text: This creature resembles a mysterious Pokémon that, according to a paranormal magazine, has lived since ancient times.

985.name: Scream Tail
985.flavor_text: It resembles a mysterious Pokémon described in a paranormal magazine as a Jigglypuff from one billion years ago.

986.name: Brute Bonnet
986.flavor_text: It bears a slight resemblance to a Pokémon described in a dubious magazine as a cross between a dinosaur and a mushroom.

987.name: Flutter Mane
987.flavor_text: It has similar features to a ghostly pterosaur that was covered in a paranormal magazine, but the two have little else in common.

988.name: Slither Wing
988.flavor_text: This Pokémon somewhat resembles an ancient form of Volcarona that was introduced in a dubious magazine.

989.name: Sandy Shocks
989.flavor_text: It slightly resembles a Magneton that lived for 10,000 years and was featured in an article in a paranormal magazine.

990.name: Iron Treads
990.flavor_text: Sightings of this Pokémon have occurred in recent years. It resembles a mysterious object described in an old expedition journal.

991.name: Iron Bundle
991.flavor_text: It resembles a mysterious object mentioned in an old book. There are only two reported sightings of this Pokémon.

992.name: Iron Hands
992.flavor_text: This Pokémon shares many similarities with Iron Hands, an object mentioned in a certain expedition journal.

993.name: Iron Jugulis
993.flavor_text: It’s possible that Iron Jugulis, an object described in an old book, may actually be this Pokémon.

994.name: Iron Moth
994.flavor_text: No records exist of this species being caught. Data is lacking, but the Pokémon’s traits match up with an object described in an old book.

995.name: Iron Thorns
995.flavor_text: Some of its notable features match those of an object named within a certain expedition journal as Iron Thorns.

996.name: Frigibax
996.flavor_text: This Pokémon lives in forests and craggy areas. Using the power of its dorsal fin, it cools the inside of its nest like a refrigerator.

997.name: Arctibax
997.flavor_text: It attacks with the blade of its frozen dorsal fin by doing a front flip in the air. Arctibax’s strong back and legs allow it to pull off this technique.

998.name: Baxcalibur
998.flavor_text: It launches itself into battle by flipping upside down and spewing frigid air from its mouth. It finishes opponents off with its dorsal blade.

999.name: Gimmighoul
999.flavor_text: It lives inside an old treasure chest. Sometimes it gets left in shop corners since no one realizes it’s actually a Pokémon.

1000.name: Gholdengo
1000.flavor_text: It has a sturdy body made up of stacked coins. Gholdengo overwhelms its enemies by firing coin after coin at them in quick succession.

1001.name: Wo Chien
1001.flavor_text: It drains the life-force from vegetation, causing nearby forests to instantly wither and fields to turn barren.

1002.name: Chien Pao
1002.flavor_text: The hatred of those who perished by the sword long ago has clad itself in snow and become a Pokémon.

1003.name: Ting Lu
1003.flavor_text: It slowly brings its exceedingly heavy head down upon the ground, splitting the earth open with huge fissures that run over 160 feet deep.

1004.name: Chi Yu
1004.flavor_text: The envy accumulated within curved beads that sparked multiple conflicts has clad itself in fire and become a Pokémon.

1005.name: Roaring Moon
1005.flavor_text: According to an article in a dubious magazine, this Pokémon has some connection to a phenomenon that occurs in a certain region.

1006.name: Iron Valiant
1006.flavor_text: It’s possible that this is the object listed as Iron Valiant in a certain expedition journal.

1007.name: Koraidon
1007.flavor_text: This Pokémon resembles Cyclizar, but it is far burlier and more ferocious. Nothing is known about its ecology or other features.

1008.name: Miraidon
1008.flavor_text: This seems to be the Iron Serpent mentioned in an old book. The Iron Serpent is said to have turned the land to ash with its lightning.

1009.name: Walking Wake
1009.flavor_text: It resembles an illustration published in a paranormal magazine, said to be a depiction of a super-ancient Suicune.

1010.name: Iron Leaves
1010.flavor_text: According to the few eyewitness accounts that exist, it used its shining blades to julienne large trees and boulders.

1011.name: Dipplin
1011.flavor_text: The head sticking out belongs to the fore-wyrm, while the tail belongs to the core-wyrm. The two share one apple and help each other out.

1012.name: Poltchageist
1012.flavor_text: Poltchageist looks like a regional form of Sinistea, but it was recently discovered that the two Pokémon are entirely unrelated.

1013.name: Sinistcha
1013.flavor_text: It prefers cool, dark places, such as the back of a shelf or the space beneath a home's floorboards. It wanders in search of prey after sunset.

1014.name: Okidogi
1014.flavor_text: Okidogi is a ruffian with a short temper. It can pulverize anything by swinging around the chain on its neck.

1015.name: Munkidori
1015.flavor_text: Munkidori keeps itself somewhere safe while it toys with its foes, using psychokinesis to induce intense dizziness.

1016.name: Fezandipiti
1016.flavor_text: Fezandipiti beats its glossy wings to scatter pheromones that captivate people and Pokémon.

1017.name: Ogerpon
1017.flavor_text: This mischief-loving Pokémon is full of curiosity. It battles by drawing out the type-based energy contained within its masks.

1018.name: Archaludon
1018.flavor_text: It digs holes on mountains, searching for food. It’s so durable that being caught in a cave-in won’t faze it.

1019.name: Hydrapple
1019.flavor_text: These capricious syrpents have banded together. On the rare occasion that their moods align, their true power is unleashed.

1020.name: Gouging Fire
1020.flavor_text: It resembles an eerie Pokémon once shown in a paranormal magazine. That Pokémon was said to be an Entei regenerated from a fossil.

1021.name: Raging Bolt
1021.flavor_text: It bears resemblance to a Pokémon that became a hot topic for a short while after a paranormal magazine touted it as Raikou's ancestor.

1022.name: Iron Boulder
1022.flavor_text: It was named after a mysterious object recorded in an old book. Its body seems to be metallic.

1023.name: Iron Crown
1023.flavor_text: There was supposedly an incident in which it launched shining blades to cut everything around it to pieces. Little else is known about it.

1024.name: Terapagos
1024.flavor_text: It’s thought that this Pokémon lived in ancient Paldea until it got caught in seismic shifts and went extinct.

1025.name: Pecharunt
1025.flavor_text: Its peach-shaped shell serves as storage for a potent poison. It makes poisonous mochi and serves them to people and Pokémon.
